messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,
the second picture also does not contain date and time. I suspect that in uploading to the google group the image is stripped of its metadata.

To answer the question, the errors arose because images don't store the date/time tag correctly (telling from images emailed to me, not the images uploaded to the google group). The date/time information is not in the Exif metadata slot DateTimeOriginal, but instead in XMP:DateTimeOriginal. This can be checked with exiftool like this (the -G argument makes exiftool return the tag group name):

exiftool -G "C:\Path\to\your\images\Tagged - not working.jpg"

I don't know how and why this happened. It is weird because it should be saved in the right place by default (except for some specific reconyx camera models).

Anyways, here is a method for fixing this problem. Please be sure to make a backup first. And replace  "C:\Path\to\your\images" with the path to your images (only the images with this date/time problem!).  Run the lines beginning with exiftool in the command line (cmd.exe in Windows)

1. Fix the metadata problems (this does not yet work on the DateTimeOriginal tag)

exiftool -all= -tagsfromfile @ -all:all -unsafe -icc_profile  "C:\Path\to\your\images"

2. Create an Exif:DateTimeOriginal tag from the XMP:DateTimeOriginal tag

exiftool "-EXIF:DateTimeOriginal<XMP:DateTimeOriginal" "C:\Path\to\your\images"

# then delete the jpg_original files if the result is ok (manually or with this line)
exiftool -delete_original "C:\Path\to\your\images"

For 4000 images it may take a while.
If you want to run it recursively (including all subdirectories of the directory you give, add "-r", e.g.:

exiftool -all= -tagsfromfile @ -all:all -unsafe -icc_profile -r "C:\Path\to\your\images"

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: ProblemX_From ProblemX_To
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the ProblemX_From, ProblemX_To columns are not made for this kind of problem. It is for situations in which a camera stopped working altogether for a period of time.

>From what I see you have two choices, depending on what the ratio of good vs bad images is:

1) if only few black images, just treat the camera like it worked fine (basically ignore the black images)
2) if many black images and you think you missed many sightings, exclude the station from your analyses.

Unfortunately, the package currently has no way of correcting for this sort of problem automatically.
However, if you run occupancy or spatial capture-recapture analyses, you could manually correct the effort matrix by multiplying whatvever value you have in there for that station by the ratio of good / bad images. Then include effort in your models as a detection covariate.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: 'date.test. in detection histories
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the main problem is your argument day1 = "setup".
You have 3 options for argument day1. it can be "station", "survey", or a date, formatted like this: "2016-12-31". "setup" is not possible. I will add a proper error message for this case. The object date.test is used in internal tests of the function and should not be visible.

Besides this,  occasionStartTime needs to be defined differently.
occasionStartTime = 00:00 will work, but only by chance. In R, the colon : is a shorthand for a sequence of numbers. Thus 00:00 means: sequence from 0 to 0 (which is 0) and will thus work. If you set it to e.g. 06:00 it will be a sequence from 6 to 0 (equivalent to c(6,5,4,3,2,1,0) and seq(6,0)) and will not work in this function), The correct way to use the argment occasionStartTime is to give a single number. If you want midnight, it is occasionStartTime = 0 and if you want 12 noon, it is occasionStartTime = 12.

messages.body_plain:
I keep getting an error. I am running the appendSpeciesNames in the camtrapR package. This systematically goes through all of the photo's I have in a directory and adds my species name into the file name from the metadata.
The code I use is this.

     checkSpeciesIdentification(inDir = "SECRimagesOUT",
                                             IDfrom = "metadata",
                                             hasCameraFolders = FALSE,
                                             metadataSpeciesTag = "Species"
                                             metadataHeirarchyDelimitor = "|",
                                             removeNames = FALSE,
                                             writecsv = FALSE)

 It works fine until I get to the 7th folder and then I get this warning:

     Warning: out 07: metadataSpeciesTag 'Species' not found in image metadata tag 'Hierarchicalsubject'.

Followed by this error.

     Error in rep(dirs_short[i], times =nrow(metadata.tmp)) : invalid 'times' argument

I'm pretty sure this error is referring to line 146 of the code in this link:

https://github.com/cran/camtrapR/blob/master/R/appendSpeciesNames.R

But here is a copy paste of the line of code I think the error is referring to:

      metadata.tmp <- cbind(station = rep(dirs_short[i], times = nrow(metadata.tmp)), metadata.tmp)

The exact same code for another directory (inDir = "SECRimagesIN") works perfectly.

When I tried a different function for the same image directory I have the error with, I get caught out at the exact same folder before a different error occurs.

        checkSpeciesIdentification(inDir = "SECRimagesOUT",
                                             IDfrom = "metadata",
                                             hasCameraFolders = FALSE,
                                             metadataSpeciesTag = "Species"
                                             metadataHeirarchyDelimitor = "|",
                                             maxDeltaTime = 5,
                                             writecsv = FALSE)
The error in this instance is

      error: $operator is invalid for atomic vectors.

But it comes with the same warning message.

The only thing that is different about his folder is that there are no images with the "Species' tag that I specify with the metadataSpeciesTag argument. When I add a species tag to even just one image it seems to work only to be caught up at the next folder that lacks an image with the "Species" tag.

Does anyone have any suggestions. Is the function only able to deal with a directory that has the tag in each of the folders? If so is there an alternative?

Cheers

messages.subject: Re: Error in appendSpeciesNames
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shannon,
well spotted. Thank you. You answered you question already. This is a bug that occurs when trying to extract metadata species IDs and no image in a station directory has a species tag, So far only the function recordTable handled this situation (see this related post <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/camtrapr/I6FR6ETestU>), but from the next release on all functions that extract species IDs from metadata will handle this situation by giving a warning and skipping the station.
A quick fix would be to assign a species tag to at least one image per directory. But this is of course nothing but a emergency solution.

Please see the attached files. They contain the two functions in question (appendSpeciesNames and checkSpeciesIdentification) plus another file containing some helper funcitons. Run them all and then try again with your directories without species tags.

One more minor thing, probably just a copy&paste mistake. In your first function call above, you probably mean appendSpeciesNames, not checkSpeciesIdentification. Besides, there is a typo in your function call (see below) and arguments metadataHierarchyDelimitor, removeNames and writecsv don't need to be included in the function call because you use the defaut of those arguments.

     appendSpeciesNames(inDir = "SECRimagesOUT",

                        IDfrom = "metadata",
                        hasCameraFolders = FALSE,
                        metadataSpeciesTag = "Species"

                        metadataHierarchyDelimitor= "|",

                        removeNames = FALSE,
                        writecsv = FALSE)

Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: 'date.test. in detection histories
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
this error is unrelated to the error you had earlier. It arises because the camera operation matrix is not in the format expected by the function detectionHistory. I suppose you load the camera operation matrix from your hard disk after saving it? By default, saving and loading a data frame with the default settings will change the data frame. The row names will become a distinct column. That column has no name and therefore R calls it "X", as happened in your case above.

You can do two different things:

1. run cameraOperation() anew and use the matrix the function gives you instead of an object that was saved as a file
2. load the file with two additional arguments:  write.csv(..., rownames = 1, check.names = FALSE)

The package vignette also mentions this issue briefly: see here <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/DataExtraction.html#saving-and-loading-camera-operation-matrices>.

Best regards,
Jürgen
